newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Two killed in tribal clash in Nigerian oil city.
newsitem.headline: Two killed in tribal clash in Nigerian oil city.

text.p: Two people were killed and three wounded in fighting between youths of rival tribes in the Nigerian oil city of Warri, local newspapers reported on Friday.
They said the latest clash took place on Thursday, a day after army commanders deployed in the troubled city had reached an agreement with local community leaders to maintain peace.
One of the victims, a woman, was hit by a stray bullet fired by soldiers trying to disperse the youths, the semi-official Daily Times newspaper said.
Scores of people have died in the clashes in Warri, which began in mid-March over the relocation of the local government council from an Ijaw town to that of the rival Itsekiri tribe.

At the height of the crisis, oil production by the Nigerian unit of Royal Dutch Shell Group was affected but all except one of the oil flow stations the company shut down at the time because of the crisis have since been reopened.
A Shell spokesman in Lagos said the company's operations had not been affected by Thursday's fighting.
"It wasn't anywhere near where we operate. Our operations are coninuing as normal," he added.
A military spokesman in Lagos said the clash appeared to have been an isolated incident and there had been no report of it continuing on Friday.
